prosecutions.title: Missing explicit error taxonomy across auth/session/data/privacy boundaries
failure_risks: AI-generated handlers collapse distinct failures into generic errors, causing incorrect auto-retry/logout decisions.
Cross-boundary error translation drifts, producing incompatible behavior between routes, providers, and service facades.
Observability becomes noisy and non-actionable because semantic failure classes are absent.
prosecutions.prosecutor_argument: Local handling is not a substitute for cross-boundary contracts. In worst-case automated refactors, missing taxonomy amplifies regressions and makes recovery logic unsafe.

prosecutions.title: Silent-failure risk from multi-layer fallback chains (crypto + cache + offline)
failure_risks: Fallbacks succeed superficially while privacy posture downgrades without user-visible signal.
Cache/offline fallback returns stale data that AI-generated UI treats as authoritative truth.
Partial persistence appears successful, creating hidden divergence between local state and backend state.
prosecutions.prosecutor_argument: Continuity without explicit degraded-mode signaling is indistinguishable from correctness. Worst-case, the app silently violates user expectations and data guarantees.

prosecutions.title: Inconsistent error propagation between client provider, service facades, and API routes
failure_risks: AI patches introduce mixed throw/nullable/HTTP error conventions that break caller assumptions.
Identical backend failures trigger divergent UX outcomes depending on call path.
Error swallowing in one layer prevents upper-layer compensating logic from executing.
prosecutions.prosecutor_argument: Layer-specific contracts are valid only when explicitly mapped. Without a unifying propagation policy, variation becomes unbounded defect surface.

prosecutions.title: Import/export pipeline likely lacks partial-failure semantics
failure_risks: Bulk import reports success while dropping conflicted/encrypted subsets silently.
Retries duplicate previously successful sub-operations due to missing resumability markers.
AI-generated migration/import code cannot classify retryable vs terminal failures, causing data corruption loops.
prosecutions.prosecutor_argument: Whole-operation simplicity fails under real-world fault patterns. Worst-case imports become non-auditable and irrecoverable.

prosecutions.title: Unused dual-service architecture (`simple` vs `cached`) increases error drift
failure_risks: AI modifies one facade only, creating semantic drift in validation, nullability, and retries.
Feature toggling or accidental callsite usage flips behavior unexpectedly between facades.
Bug fixes appear complete in tests that target one facade but fail in production paths using the other.
prosecutions.prosecutor_argument: Interim dual facades require strict convergence controls. Without them, worst-case AI edits create split-brain service behavior.

prosecutions.title: Auth refresh/validation loop lacks explicit retry budget and terminal states
failure_risks: Network flaps cause unbounded validate-refresh oscillation and request storms.
Session races produce contradictory UI states (authenticated vs forced logout).
AI-introduced retries bypass intended guard conditions, resulting in account lockouts or token churn.
prosecutions.prosecutor_argument: Implicit guards are fragile under concurrent and degraded conditions. Worst-case auth control flow needs explicit terminal states and retry budgets.

prosecutions.title: Cache subsystem breadth can mask cache-write/cache-invalidate failures
failure_risks: Invalidation misses are treated as benign, yielding long-lived stale UI decisions.
AI-generated mutations forget one invalidation branch, causing correctness bugs that evade basic tests.
Operational incidents are harder to triage because cache outcomes are not first-class telemetry.
prosecutions.prosecutor_argument: Non-fatal cache strategy does not justify invisible cache failures. In worst-case evolution, stale correctness defects become systemic.

prosecutions.title: SSR mock cache adapters risk diverging failure semantics from browser runtime
failure_risks: SSR passes while browser runtime fails due to mocked success semantics.
Hydration transitions expose state mismatches that were hidden by SSR no-op adapters.
AI-written tests overfit SSR behavior and miss real client-side cache fault paths.
prosecutions.prosecutor_argument: Exact parity may be impractical, but semantic compatibility is mandatory for reliability. Worst-case divergence invalidates confidence from SSR-centric testing.

prosecutions.title: "Class + singleton + bound exports" obscures ownership of throw/catch boundaries
failure_risks: AI refactors patch one invocation style and leave others with stale error normalization.
Stack traces and ownership boundaries become ambiguous, delaying incident resolution.
Duplicate entry points allow inconsistent instrumentation and policy enforcement.
prosecutions.prosecutor_argument: Legacy compatibility cannot justify opaque error ownership indefinitely. Worst-case complexity increases the chance of unreviewed boundary regressions.

prosecutions.title: Placeholder options/no-op API paths can imply successful handling when none occurred
failure_risks: Callers assume options were applied when runtime silently ignored them.
AI-generated features rely on placeholders and ship with false-positive success paths.
No-op behavior suppresses alarms, delaying detection of missing implementation.
prosecutions.prosecutor_argument: Compatibility shims are acceptable only with explicit signaling and deprecation controls. Silent no-ops are functionally equivalent to correctness failure.

prosecutions.title: Cache invalidation rule set includes non-active operations, diluting failure signal clarity
failure_risks: Inactive branches create noise that obscures real invalidation regressions.
AI contributors copy speculative rules into new mutations without runtime validation.
Debugging time increases because rule intent and operational reality diverge.
prosecutions.prosecutor_argument: Future-proofing via speculative rules must not degrade present observability. Worst-case, signal dilution conceals real cache coherence defects.

overall_verdict.summary: Under worst-case AI coding scenarios, every defended slop remains materially risky; all defenses are challenged due to high regression amplification, silent degradation potential, and weak boundary contracts.
